newsitem.title: USA: N.H. Gov. proposes GO bonds for kindergarten plan.
newsitem.headline: N.H. Gov. proposes GO bonds for kindergarten plan.

text.p: New Hampshire Gov. Jeanne Shaheen Tuesday proposed issuing $30 million in state general obligation bonds over the next five years, part of her effort to end New Hampshire's status as the only state without mandatory public kindergarten.
Shaheen, a Democrat, has promised to make public kindergarten available to every five-year old in New Hampshire.

Her next step, expected in her operating budget Thursday, is to increase funds for operating kindergarten and, legislative insiders say, distribute them through a formula that would help poorer towns with high local property tax rates.
Under the plan, which must be approved by the Legislature, the state would issue annual general obligation bonds for the five fiscal years from 1998 to 2002.

Communities would receive grants for education construction, covering 100 percent of expenditures for communities without kindergarten and 75 percent of new construction costs for communities that already have kindergarten.

"We have talked about kindergarten long enough," Shaheen said at Chichester Central School, in a small town that has not been able to afford kindergarten. "On Thursday this rhetoric ends when I present a budget that makes kindergarten a real priority in New Hampshire."
New Hampshire's state general obligation debt is rated AA by Moody's Investors Services Inc., and AA plus Fitch Investors Service and Standard & Poors.
